We got many templates, but need the one that corresponds to intramolecular Michael addition cyclization of chalcone to flavanone. Look at the first result (reaction_id 162961). The mapped_rxn shows product is flavanone-like? Let's examine product_smiles: '[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][c:4]1[cH:5][cH:6][c:7]([CH:8]2[C:9](=[O:10])[O:11][c:12]3[c:13]2[cH:14][c:15]([CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]3)[cH:19][cH:20]1' This looks like a phenoxy side chain with a carbonyl and a cyclic structure maybe flavanone. Reactant_smiles: 'O[CH:8]([c:7]1[cH:6][cH:5][c:4]([O:3][CH2:2][CH3:1])[cH:20][cH:19]1)[C:9](O)=[O:10].[OH:11][c:12]1[cH:13][cH:14][c:15]([CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1' This looks like a phenol (aryl hydroxyl) and a carbonyl (ketone). This matches chalcone? The reaction appears to form a cyclic product with an ether oxygen (O-CH2 linking). So likely this is the correct template.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The template_id is likely the reaction_id? Or there is separate template_id field? In search results, each entry includes reaction_id and template_hash. The template_id used to search is probably the reaction_id? The description says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". In earlier tasks, template_id likely corresponds to reaction_id. So we can use reaction_id 162961.

Thus answer: {'mapped_rxn': '[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][c:4]1[cH:5][cH:6][c:7]([CH:8]2[C:9](=[O:10])[O:11][c:12]3[c:13]2[cH:14][c:15]([CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]3)[cH:19][cH:20]1', 'template_id': 162961}
